correctness.rationale: For s states, k input symbols, and total transition-output length L, the standard encoding length is at least 2L+4s. Since n=|T(p)|<=kL, AM-GM gives 2L+k>=2sqrt(2n). Thus every description costs at least 2sqrt(2n)+4s>=2sqrt(2n)+4. For n=2a^2, a one-state transducer with loop outputs 0^a and epsilon, on input 0^(2a), has cost (2a+4)+2a=4a+4, matching the lower bound. Equality in the real lower bound requires 2n to be a square; because it is even, n=2a^2.

The result gives exact values for infinitely many naturally defined constant words and identifies where a universal storage-versus-input lower bound is attained. It sharpens a previously known Theta(sqrt(n)) estimate without claiming a formula for every n.
